svg.title: SpiralCore transport with ternary tree binders
svg.desc: Three parts. Left: a three-branch tree of atoms with one root-to-leaf path highlighted, and below it the 16 roots of one E8 anchor orbit drawn as nodes joined by 15 edges. As a query point moves, its nearest root changes, and the chosen atom's 8 coordinates travel along the edges between the two roots, each edge permuting axes and flipping signs; the same path run backward is the exact inverse, each step cubed. Middle: a worked example on the root with 1 in axes 0 and 1: edge B0 moves the two non-zero values to axes 4 and 2, edge B1 moves them to axes 6 and 5 with sign flips, and the two steps composed into one signed action give the same final vector. Right: a dense grid where every input block connects to every output block beside a grid where each output block reads exactly one chosen atom, labelled with the atom number.
svg.text: SpiralCore transport: each output reads one atom, moved by exact signed swaps
1 Choose an atom, move it along edges
Tree of atoms: 3 children per node, one path chosen
Its 8 coordinates travel along the edges:
16 roots of one E8 anchor orbit
joined by 15 SpiralCore edges B (each B² = −I)
Layout is schematic: which roots touch which edge is
not drawn from the source graph.
2 Two edges on a real vector
Composed into one signed action A
A = B1 · B0: axis 0 → 5, axis 1 → 6, both −
A applied to the start vector
All 8 axes move at each edge; only the two
non-zero values are drawn. No coefficient is
exactly one atom, and there is no
Tree, ring layout, atom choices and grid sizes are schematic. The 8-vector example is computed from the SpiralCore octonion table. Status: ready.
